candidate.answerReason: On a standard die, rolling a 1 and rolling a 2 cannot happen together, but outcomes 3 through 6 belong to neither event. Thus the events are mutually exclusive without being complementary.

methods.label: Give a counterexample
methods.explanation: Both events may fail to occur. For example, when rolling a die, “rolling a 1” and “rolling a 2” are mutually exclusive but not complementary.
methods.levelReason: Uses the definitions and one elementary counterexample to refute an always statement.
